findings.title: Costs
findings.text: Slippage and commissions cost 0.069R per trade on average (+0.001R before costs, -0.068R after). Before costs the setups made money; costs erase it.

findings.title: Win rate vs what's needed
findings.text: Win rate 37.3% against about 39.9% needed to break even with the actual average winner (+1.54R) and loser (-1.02R). Median target was 2.0R; only 21.3% of trades ever reached +2R before exiting.

findings.title: False breakouts
findings.text: 30.5% of stopped trades were stopped within 2 bars of entry: the move reversed almost immediately. Not unusually high.

findings.title: Giving back winners
findings.text: 17.6% of losing trades were up at least +1R at some point before turning into a loss. Few losers were ever meaningfully profitable, so exit management isn't the main problem.

findings.title: Stop placement
findings.text: 11.5% of stopped trades went on to reach the original target later the same day; 50.0% of those never went more than 1.5R against the entry first, so a somewhat wider stop might have held. Wider stops mean smaller positions, so this is a trade-off to test, not a fix.

findings.title: Long vs short
findings.text: Best: short +0.131R over 405 trades (95% interval [-0.153, 0.39]). Worst: long -0.277R over 384 trades (interval [-0.432, -0.14]).

findings.title: Trading with or against the trend
findings.text: Best: with trend +0.032R over 427 trades (95% interval [-0.117, 0.194]). Worst: against trend -0.239R over 249 trades (interval [-0.408, -0.05]).

findings.title: Time of day
findings.text: Best: 11:30-14:00 midday -0.012R over 274 trades (95% interval [-0.154, 0.152]). Worst: 14:00-16:00 afternoon -0.198R over 177 trades (interval [-0.366, -0.002]).

findings.title: Choppy markets
findings.text: Best: choppy / consolidating -0.044R over 112 trades (95% interval [-0.263, 0.168]). Worst: trending / expanding -0.072R over 677 trades (interval [-0.203, 0.076]).

findings.title: Late / extended entries
findings.text: Best: extended (>1.5 ATR from 9 EMA) +0.023R over 157 trades (95% interval [-0.341, 0.399]). Worst: near 9 EMA (<=1.5 ATR) -0.090R over 632 trades (interval [-0.195, 0.012]).

findings.title: Volume confirmation
findings.text: Best: volume confirmed +0.004R over 123 trades (95% interval [-0.35, 0.329]). Worst: weak volume -0.081R over 666 trades (interval [-0.193, 0.038]).

findings.title: Volatility
findings.text: Best: high-vol -0.032R over 317 trades (95% interval [-0.255, 0.181]). Worst: normal-vol -0.092R over 472 trades (interval [-0.185, 0.014]).

findings.title: Checklist score
findings.text: Best: checklist >= 70 +0.004R over 207 trades (95% interval [-0.222, 0.211]). Worst: checklist < 50 -0.158R over 319 trades (interval [-0.327, 0.015]).

findings.title: Setups that clearly lose
findings.text: failed_breakdown (long) (-0.349R, 130 trades); level_breakout (long) (-0.396R, 74 trades); vwap_reclaim (long) (-0.564R, 47 trades). These are switched to NO TRADE in live signals.

findings.title: Setups with positive evidence
findings.text: None. No setup or ticker slice has an out-of-sample 95% interval entirely above zero.

diagnostics.caveat: These slices describe past out-of-sample trades. Choosing filters from them and re-testing on the same trades would be curve-fitting; any idea here must be confirmed on later data.

search.note: Each fold tried 12 parameter combinations on its training window and kept the best. The more combinations tried, the more the training winner is a lucky draw - which is exactly why only the following, unseen test window is reported.
